title: Communication Strategy and Operations Planner (I) (LtCol to Capt) NMOS (4502), DIR COMM
raw_text:
3. MOS 4505, Communication Strategy and Operations Planner (I) (LtCol to
Capt) NMOS (4502), DIR COMM

    a. Summary. The Communication Strategy and Operations (COMMSTRAT)
Planner is the 45XX occupational field (OccFld) subject matter expert in
formal research methods and design, advanced planning, and evaluation of
communication effects. Typical duties include, but are not limited to
advising commanders and staffs on communication research and assessment
matters, leading communication planning, conducting formal research to obtain
and analyze qualitative and quantitative data related to identifying and
segmenting audiences, publics, and stakeholders’ knowledge, attitudes, and
behaviors, supporting information environment (IE) battlespace awareness
through non-reactive research methods, incorporating research findings and
communication theory into planning and decision-making.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must possess PMOS 4502.

        (2) Must be selected by the Commandant’s Career Level Education Board
(CCLEB) or Commandant’s Professional Intermediate-Level Education Board
(CPIB).

    c. Requirements. Must successfully complete the graduate education
program and possess a master's degree in Mass Communication and Media Studies
from San Diego State University.

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to the
Communication Strategy and Operations Training and Readiness Manual (NAVMC
3500.9C).

       e.   Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code

            (1) Public Relations Managers 11-2032.

            (2) Training and Development Managers 11-3042.

            (3) Market Research Analysts and Marketing Specialists 13-1161.

            (4) Survey Researchers 19-3022.

            (6) Media and Communication Workers, All Other 27-3099.

       f.   Related Military Skill.   None.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
